findings.note: Owner 2026-09-10 #145 option A, now that the LANE exists. The builder withheld this row because GrantedStrike declared `die`/`damageType` required and build.ts copied both onto the NaturalAttack through stepDie, so a Web row shipped then would have rendered a Strike with an invented damage die. This gap run made a damageless granted attack expressible end to end: `GrantedStrike.die`/`damageType` are optional (src/rules/types.ts), collectGrantedNaturals no longer steps an absent die (src/rules/build.ts), applyUnarmedRiders no longer enlarges one (the level-7 animal-instinct die step would have given the Web a d4), and deriveUnarmedStrike prints "no damage" and drops every damage rider for one (src/rules/derive.ts). `onHit` is the new carrier for the printed Speed penalty, rendered onto the same damage cell as "(on a hit, …)" - GrantedStrike had no on-hit field at all and StrikeDamageRider carries damage only. The whole 31-entry array is re-emitted unchanged with the Web appended, because one member of one field cannot be patched.

backfillRows.why: instinct-8's animal table prints the spider with TWO attacks - "Spider Fangs 1d8 P Grapple, unarmed, venomous Web Special Range increment 15 feet" - and the footnote "The spider's web attack deals no damage, but the target takes a -10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round on a hit." Only Fangs shipped, so a spider barbarian was missing half of what Bestial Rage grants: "While raging, you gain your chosen animal's unarmed attack (or attacks)". The Web carries no die and no damageType (the printed damage column is "Special", i.e. none), a 15-foot range increment, and the printed penalty as `onHit`. Every one of the superseded row's 31 entries is merged in byte-identical; only the Web is added.

value.name: Web
value.onHit: the target takes a -10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round

findings.note: The occult twin of kitsune-spell-familiarity, whose row data-rows-5 authored; this is the same shape with the same reasoning. The record already asked the question at daily preparations (choice.daily), but its three options carried no `grant`, so dailyChoiceGrants (derive.ts) produced nothing and the answer changed nothing - the only live control was the BUILD-TIME picker in FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS, which print does not have. That registry entry is deleted in this same gap run (src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts), so the two must land together: with only the deletion the feat grants nothing, with only the row it asks twice. The rank-0 half of the reader landed with data-rows-5's play.ts change (a daily-granted cantrip now joins the innate entry's `cantrips` list instead of being dropped by `if (rank <= 0) continue`). The whole `choice` value is re-emitted because a member of one field cannot be patched.

backfillRows.why: feat-3984 prints "During your daily preparations, choose daze , detect magic , or mage hand . Until your next daily preparations, you can cast the chosen spell as an occult innate cantrip. A cantrip is heightened to a spell level equal to half your level rounded up." (mage hand is now Telekinetic Hand, which is why the third option is telekinetic-hand). `atWill` with no rank is the innate-cantrip shape - cast at will, auto-heightened - so the printed heightening falls out of the lane rather than being frozen at a number. The superseded row's whole value (flag/prompt/kind/daily/options, same order, same labels) is merged in unchanged; only `grant` and a per-option `description` are added.
